title: The Council with the Munchkins, part 4
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: “Then that accounts for it. In the civilized countries I believe there are no witches left, nor wizards, nor sorceresses, nor magicians. But, you see, the Land of Oz has never been civilized, for we are cut off from all the rest of the world. Therefore we still have witches and wizards amongst us.”
“Oz himself is the Great Wizard,” answered the Witch, sinking her voice to a whisper. “He is more powerful than all the rest of us together. He lives in the City of Emeralds.”

Dorothy was going to ask another question, but just then the Munchkins, who had been standing silently by, gave a loud shout and pointed to the corner of the house where the Wicked Witch had been lying.
“What is it?” asked the little old woman, and looked, and began to laugh. The feet of the dead Witch had disappeared entirely, and nothing was left but the silver shoes.

“She was so old,” explained the Witch of the North, “that she dried up quickly in the sun. That is the end of her. But the silver shoes are yours, and you shall have them to wear.” She reached down and picked up the shoes, and after shaking the dust out of them handed them to Dorothy.
“The Witch of the East was proud of those silver shoes,” said one of the Munchkins, “and there is some charm connected with them; but what it is we never knew.”
Dorothy carried the shoes into the house and placed them on the table. Then she came out again to the Munchkins and said:
“I am anxious to get back to my aunt and uncle, for I am sure they will worry about me. Can you help me find my way?”
The Munchkins and the Witch first looked at one another, and then at Dorothy, and then shook their heads.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who is the Great Wizard?
options: Oz himself
The Witch of the North
The eldest of the Munchkins
The Wicked Witch of the West

questions.prompt: Per the passage, where does the Great Wizard live?
options: In the City of Emeralds
In the land of the East
Beyond the great desert
In the country of the Winkies

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to the dead Witch's feet?
options: They dried up in the sun and disappeared
They were carried away by the Munchkins
They were buried beneath the fallen house
They turned to silver along with the shoes

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did Dorothy do with the silver shoes?
options: Carried them inside and put them on the table
Put them straight on and walked about in them
Gave them to the little old woman to keep safe
Left them lying in the dust where they had fallen

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Dorothy ask the Munchkins to help her do?
options: Find her way back to her aunt and uncle
Carry her house back to the prairie
Bury the witch her house had fallen on
Reach the City of Emeralds before dark

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Land of Oz still have witches and wizards?
options: It is cut off from the rest of the world and never was civilized
Its people have refused to give up the customs of their fathers
The Great Wizard gathers them there and will not let them leave
The desert around it draws them in from the civilized countries

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what do the Munchkins know about the silver shoes?
options: That some charm belongs to them, but not what it is
That whoever wears them cannot be harmed by witches
That they were made by the Great Wizard as a gift
That they will carry the wearer across the desert

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the shaking of heads tell Dorothy?
options: That nobody there can help her get home
That she has asked a forbidden question
That they do not believe she wants to leave
That the Wizard alone may be spoken to

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, why does the Witch sink her voice to a whisper?
options: She drops it low in speaking of the Wizard
She has grown hoarse from so much talking
She wants the Munchkins to come nearer
She is afraid Dorothy will refuse to listen

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures what the passage does?
options: It names the one power that might send Dorothy home, and gives her the shoes
It explains how the Wicked Witch of the East first came to rule the East
It shows the Munchkins deciding which of them will guide Dorothy
It describes the City of Emeralds and the road that leads to it

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how powerful is Oz said to be?
options: More powerful than all the rest of them together
About as powerful as the Witch of the North
Less powerful than the Wicked Witch of the West
Powerful only within the walls of his own city

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Munchkins do that interrupted Dorothy's next question?
options: They gave a loud shout and pointed at the house
They began to weep and take out handkerchiefs
They bowed low and walked away through the trees
They picked up the shoes and handed them over

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was left of the Wicked Witch of the East?
options: Nothing but the silver shoes
Nothing but a block of wood
Nothing but her pointed hat
Nothing but a mark in the dust

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the Witch of the North laugh at the sight?
options: The witch had simply dried up, and that was the end of her
The Munchkins had been frightened by their own shouting
Dorothy had jumped back from the corner of the house
The shoes had been left behind exactly as she foretold

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does Dorothy most want at this point?
options: To get back to the aunt and uncle who will be worrying
To learn what charm the silver shoes are said to carry
To meet the Great Wizard who lives in the Emerald City
To see the rest of the beautiful country she has landed in

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does the Witch mean by a civilized country?
options: One joined to the wider world, where magic has died out
One whose people are gentle and well mannered
One large enough to hold a city and a desert
One ruled by a wizard rather than by witches

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: Dorothy is given the dead witch's shoes and asks in vain for a way home
Dorothy refuses the silver shoes and asks to meet the Wizard instead
The Munchkins explain why the Wizard will not see any stranger
The Witch of the North offers to carry Dorothy across the desert
